stem: Which mechanism best explains excess adrenal androgen production in congenital adrenal hyperplasia?

options.text: Impaired steroidogenesis causes excess ACTH signalling and shunts steroid synthesis towards adrenal androgen production
Direct pancreatic beta-cell stimulation increases adrenal androgen synthesis
Reduced ACTH signalling causes all steroid precursors to convert into cortisol
Thyroid hormone excess directly activates adrenal androgen secretion
Renal sodium loss independently drives androgen synthesis without pituitary involvement

explanation: Impaired steroidogenesis causes excess ACTH signalling and diversion of steroid precursors towards adrenal androgen production. In congenital adrenal hyperplasia, reduced cortisol synthesis removes negative feedback on the pituitary, increasing ACTH and shunting precursors into androgen pathways.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because impaired steroidogenesis reduces cortisol production, increases ACTH drive, and shunts steroid precursors towards adrenal androgen synthesis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because pancreatic beta-cell stimulation does not explain adrenal androgen excess in congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because reduced ACTH would not drive androgen excess, and the pathway does not convert all precursors into cortisol.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because thyroid hormone excess is not the mechanism for adrenal androgen overproduction in congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because renal sodium loss is not the primary driver of adrenal androgen synthesis without pituitary ACTH signalling.
